about.title: About, Sources & Methodology
about.intro: Bharat Darshan presents a standard, comparable profile for every State and Union Territory. Every figure links to its source.
about.p1: Every number stores its value, unit, period, source, link, access date, revision status and a confidence level.
about.p2: We never invent, interpolate or silently estimate figures. Unknown values show “Not available” and are listed in the data-gap report.
about.p3: Financial years, calendar years and price bases are always labelled and never mixed.
about.p4: Census 2011 is the last completed census. Current population estimates come from official projections and are labelled “Projected”.
about.p5: Officeholders, project status and election dates carry an “as of” date and a link to verify on the official site.
about.p6: Maps follow Survey of India boundaries only. Until an official file is installed, we show a boundary-free tile grid.
about.p7: Politics is presented factually and neutrally. Caste data is shown only from official published sources.
about.sourcesIntro: In order of preference within each category.

a11y.title: Accessibility & Contact
a11y.intro: We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA on every page, in every language.
items: Every page sets the correct language attribute, including text shown in another language.
All features work with a keyboard; a skip link leads to the main content.
Every map has a text and table alternative; colour is never the only way information is shown.
Text and controls meet AA contrast in both light and dark themes.
Motion is reduced when your device asks for it.
Numbers can be shown in Devanagari numerals with the १२३ toggle.
a11y.contactBody: Use “Suggest a correction” in any source box, or at the foot of every page. It opens a short form on GitHub (a free account is needed) asking what is wrong and for a link to the official source. Reports are reviewed before anything changes, and nothing is changed on the basis of an unsourced report.

compare.title: Compare States and UTs
compare.intro: A prototype comparison of official indicators, side by side with the national figure. Every row uses one period for all regions, and every value links to its source.
compare.limit: You can compare up to 4 regions at a time.
compare.better: Most favourable among the selected regions
compare.worse: Least favourable among the selected regions
compare.legend: ↑ and ↓ mark the most and least favourable value among the regions you selected, only for indicators where the direction is clear (for example, lower unemployment or higher literacy). They are not rankings of all States and UTs, and size indicators such as population or GSDP carry no marker.
compare.methodBody: Values come from the same official series for every region: Census 2011, MoSPI State accounts (base 2011-12, current prices), PLFS 2025, AISHE 2021-22, NFHS-5 (2019-21), the Sample Registration System and ISFR 2023. Where a region has no published value it shows “Not available” — nothing is estimated. Shares and real growth rates are computed from MoSPI figures and are labelled as such in the source details.
compare.more: Pick any 2 to 4 of the 36 States and UTs. To see all of them on one indicator, open Rankings.
compare.bar: Bar shows the value relative to the largest among the selected regions.
compare.groupPending: That themed comparison needs data for more regions and will open in Phase 3. Meanwhile, here is the prototype set.

rankings.title: Rankings of States and UTs
rankings.intro: Every State and UT ordered on one official indicator at a time. Each list uses a single period, every value links to its source, and regions without a published value are listed separately. Nothing is estimated.
rankings.higherBetter: Ranked from highest to lowest: a higher value is more favourable.
rankings.lowerBetter: Ranked from lowest to highest: a lower value is more favourable.
rankings.neutral: Ordered from largest to smallest. This measures size or structure, so a higher position is neither better nor worse.
rankings.coverage: {n} of {total} have a published value for {period}.
rankings.mixNote: States and UTs differ greatly in size, and not every survey covers every region. Choose “States” or “Union Territories” to rank them separately.
rankings.missingBody: No value has been published in this series for these regions. They are not ranked, and nothing is estimated.
rankings.methodBody: Ranks use the raw published values, not the rounded figures shown. Regions with the same value share a rank and the next rank is skipped (1, 2, 2, 4). Choosing States or Union Territories ranks that list on its own, so ranks change. The figures and sources are the same as on the Compare page.

glossary.title: Glossary

dataLibrary.profilesBody: One file per State or UT with everything on its profile: the region record and all 26 sections.
dataLibrary.useStatus: A value marked “not_available” has not been published in that series for that region. It is left empty on purpose and should not be filled with an estimate.
dataLibrary.useColumns: “revision_status” says whether a figure is final, provisional, revised or projected (“TODO” marks an entry still awaiting verification); “confidence” gives the kind of source behind it.
dataLibrary.useLanguages: Hindi and Marathi names and text are marked as drafts in the JSON files until a reviewer has approved them.
dataLibrary.useCite: When you reuse a figure, cite the original publisher named in its row and link to its URL.
dataLibrary.useTerms: Bharat Darshan's compilation — the selection and structure of the files, the translations and the notes — is licensed under CC BY 4.0. Credit “Bharat Darshan, CC BY 4.0” with a link to the site. The underlying figures remain under their publishers' terms.
dataLibrary.apiBody: The files are rebuilt with every update and keep the same addresses, so scripts can fetch them directly. There is no query API yet.

learn.title: Learn: quiz yourself
learn.intro: Short quizzes on India's States and UTs. Every question is built from a sourced figure or record on this site, and every answer shows where it comes from.

q.gi: Which State or UT is “{item}” registered for as a Geographical Indication?
q.office: Who is the {role} of {region}? (as checked on {date})
q.dataHigh: Among these four, which had the highest {indicator} in {period}?
q.dataLow: Among these four, which had the lowest {indicator} in {period}?
q.dataLarge: Among these four, which had the largest {indicator} in {period}?

learn.loadError: The questions could not be loaded. Please check your connection and reload the page.
learn.methodBody: Questions are generated from the site's data each time it is rebuilt, never written by hand. Officeholder questions use only cards confirmed from an official source, with the date they were checked. GI questions leave out products registered for more than one region. Number questions compare four regions on one indicator and one period, and skip any set with a tie. Rounds are drawn at random from the full bank.
